text:
Predicates:
Allowed(x) ::: Pets are allowed in building x.
DepositRequired(x) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in building x.
EqualDeposit(x) ::: The security deposit in building x is equal to one month's rent.
MoreDeposit(x) ::: The security deposit in building x is more than one month's rent.
Cat(x) ::: x is a cat.
IsCatOf(y, x) ::: x is the cat of y.
ManagedBuilding(x) ::: x is a managed building.
Rent(x, y) ::: The monthly rent at building x is $y.
MoveWith(x, y) ::: x moves in with y.
RentApartment(x, y) ::: x rents an apartment in building y.

Premises:
∃x (ManagedBuilding(x) ∧ Allowed(x)) ::: Pets are allowed in some managed buildings.
∀x (DepositRequired(x) → (EqualDeposit(x) ∨ MoreDeposit(x))) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in a managed building, and it can be either equal to one month's rent or more.
Cat(fluffy) ∧ IsCatOf(tom, fluffy) ::: Fluffy is Tom's cat. Cats are pets.
∀x (Cat(x) → Allowed(x)) ::: Cats are pets.
ManagedBuilding(oliveGarden) ::: The Olive Garden is a managed building.
Rent(oliveGarden, 2000) ::: The monthly rent at the Olive Garden is $2000.
(RentApartment(tom, oliveGarden) ↔ (MoveWith(fluffy, tom) ∧ ¬MoreDeposit(oliveGarden))) ↔ (Rent(oliveGarden, 2000) > 1500) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in a managed building if and only if he is allowed to move in with Fluffy, and the security deposit is no more than $1500. 2000$ is more than $1500.

Conclusion:
RentApartment(tom, oliveGarden) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in The Olive Garden.
